properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1@^3.0.1/@^3.6.2 and libp2p-crypto-secp256k1@~0.3.0 are real lockfile dependencies of the subgraph's dev toolchain (ganache-cli Ethereum simulator; libp2p stack used by @graphprotocol/graph-cli). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge 0.9.1 supplies the ganache/browserify PKI stack. Quantum-unsafe key transport (harvestable); migration ML-KEM-768. Present only as a toolchain dependency — replaceable by upgrading the packages that pull it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl is pulled by the dev toolchain (sshpk et al.). Ed25519 is Shor-vulnerable (deadline risk, not harvest risk); migration ML-DSA-65. Version 0.14.5 is 2017-era and unmaintained — the posture fact for the CBOM.

ECDSA over secp256k1 (and P-256/P-384) available in shipped node_modules; no call site in the subgraph mappings themselves. Library is the same logical package as LIB-a0bfbc1a.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 is a real lockfile dependency (ganache-cli/libp2p stack). X25519 scalar multiplication exposed by the shipped library; Shor-vulnerable key agreement, but no call site in the subgraph mappings — presence is the inventory question here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is Ethereum's consensus hash (pre-NIST-padding SHA-3): quantum-safe, no PQ action. Beyond the 104 artifact sites, the same lockfile this object partially covers also declares js-sha3 (Keccak-256/SHA-3 JS implementation) twice — 0.5.7 required by ethers@4.0.47 (line 2459) and ~0.8.0 for the ganache/web3 stack (entries 4259/6666/6905/6940) — the collector's keccak rule caught only the separate 'keccak' npm package (lines 3083/3205). First-party Solidity source carrying the EIP-1967 kecc

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@2.0.4 is a real declared lockfile dependency — Ethereum keystore/wallet key derivation in the ganache dev chain and graph toolchain. scrypt is memory-hard (Grover square-root only), so this is inventory rather than urgent risk; the dependency declaration is the asset. No call site in the subgraph mappings.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge 0.9.1 (dev/ganache PKI stack, known CVEs) is the collector's named source, but the lockfile ships AES through two further implementations: aes-js@3.0.0 (line 960; required at 2455 by ethers@4.0.47, a RUNTIME dependency — AES-CTR is what encrypts Ethereum keystore files) and browserify-aes@1.2.0 (line 1522; dev-only, CBC/CTR/GCM/CFB). AES is quantum-safe (Grover only); the posture fact is that three separate pure-JS AES stacks ship with this toolchain.
